title: Trump insists "we're richer now" despite report showing rising inflation
summary: CBS morning report contrasting the president's claim of no inflation and tariff-driven wealth with a CPI report showing inflation higher than when he took office.

assertions.quote: the president is by his own government's data incorrect that we don't have inflation

verdicts.note: CPI rose 3.7% year over year in the September 2026 report, well above the 2% target.
The latest release (September 2026) shows CPI-U up 0.6% on the month and 3.7% over 12 months, the fastest 12-month pace since May 2026.

assertions.quote: Inflation also jumped after those tariffs
You know what they cause? Wealth. They cause wealth. We're richer now.
inflation is higher than when he took office. It was 3% then. It's 3.7% now.

verdicts.note: CPI inflation was 3.0% in January 2025 and 3.7% in the September 2026 report.

The 12-month CPI change was 3.0% in January 2025 and 3.7% in September 2026, the latest reading; core rose from 3.3% to 2.6% over the same span, so the increase is in headline inflation driven by energy.

assertions.quote: inflation is really just eating up all of the wage growth that Trump has talked about and then some

verdicts.note: Real average hourly earnings decreased 0.7% from September 2025 to September 2026 (seasonally adjusted) as CPI growth outpaced nominal earnings growth; real weekly earnings fell 0.1%.

Derived real average hourly earnings (AHE deflated by CPI-U) show negative 12-month growth in every month from April 2026 (-0.2%) to September 2026 (-0.7%), with nominal AHE growth slowing to 3.0% while CPI ran 3.3-4.2%.

assertions.quote: Inflation also jumped after those tariffs and the Fed's target rate is 2%

verdicts.note: New York Fed estimates put the tariff contribution to consumer goods inflation at close to three points at its early-2026 peak.

By February 2026, a year after the tariffs began, they had added 2.9 percentage points to twelve-month consumer goods inflation in the sample, which would otherwise have been slightly negative; the sample excludes services, so the headline CPI contribution is smaller than the goods figure.
